video_title: Wolves Logo Reveal | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on the Timberwolves' potential to win an NBA championship
quotes.excerpt: I honestly believe if Anthony Edwards was healthy, because what people don't understand, he makes everybody on this team four to five to six percent better.
quotes.quote: It's exciting. When you look at where this team has gone, the fact that they're knocking on the door for an NBA championship. I honestly believe if Anthony Edwards was healthy, because what people don't understand, he makes everybody on this team four to five to six percent better. And it's those little incremental things that you need to get over the hump. Him not being able to perform at his maximum really hurt this team.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on why the Spurs were built to mirror the Thunder
quotes.excerpt: San Antonio was put together to mirror OKC. They play a bunch of guards. Look at their draft, all guards.
quotes.quote: San Antonio was put together to mirror OKC. They play a bunch of guards. Look at their draft, all guards. You're not going to beat the Knicks playing three or four guards. When this team is healthy, you're not going to beat this team with three or four guards because you got to figure it out.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Jaden McDaniels' potential for offensive growth
quotes.excerpt: I think Jaden McDaniels could get even better. I think he can become a better offensive player.
quotes.quote: Everybody keep talking about adding something. I want to put a little pressure on Jaden McDaniels. I think Jaden McDaniels could get even better. I think he can become a better offensive player. Now he's already a great defender, but I think offensively, he's only on the scratch of the surface of his talent. And if I was Anthony Edwards, I'd put my arms around him and say, 'While they out there looking for that number two scorer, you're right there.'

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Anthony Edwards as a modern NBA player
quotes.excerpt: He is the modern day NBA player when you look at the metrics.
quotes.quote: At his size and skill set, who can guard him? He's 6'9, 6'10, close to 6'10. He can handle, he can shoot, he can defend. He is the modern day NBA player when you look at the metrics. And all you you got to do, and it's hard to go from being a 16 point scorer to 22 points. People don't understand that mindset. You almost got to not have a conscience. You almost got to not care when you have bad games.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on why he defends Anthony Edwards' shot selection
quotes.excerpt: You're taught as a player to get away with what you can get away with.
quotes.quote: You're taught as a player to get away with what you can get away with. That's why you have three officials. So for all the people to be mad at Anthony Edwards, get mad at the people who make the call. If I can get to the free throw line 17 times and as a coach, he can do that, why am I going to encourage him to stop?

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Bill Musselman's coaching philosophy
quotes.excerpt: I'd rather die and lose because at least when you're dead, you're dead. If you live, you got to live with losing.
quotes.quote: Bill Musselman was so driven about winning. I remember he used to say to us, 'I'd rather die and lose because at least when you're dead, you're dead. If you live, you got to live with losing.' That's how he thought. And he instilled that in us.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on his reunion with Kevin Garnett
quotes.excerpt: He's the heart and soul. The reason these guys play the way they play, he did it.
quotes.quote: He's the heart and soul. The reason these guys play the way they play, he did it. His mentality. He left it on that court every night. You saw him every night. And what people don't realize, he did the same thing in practice every day.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Kevin Garnett's commitment to Minnesota
quotes.excerpt: He was loyal to a fault to this organization.
quotes.quote: Kevin Garnett had to sit him down and make him accept the trade. He did not want to leave here. He was loyal to a fault to this organization. He was like, 'Look, I'm going to win a championship here, I'm not going to win one.' He was loyal to a fault to a fault in this organization.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on Kevin Garnett's superstitions
quotes.excerpt: Kevin Garnett was very superstitious about everything.
quotes.quote: Kevin Garnett was very superstitious about everything. Everything before every game had to go in the certain order at a certain time. What he ate, what he drank, the way the hot packs were put on his knees. Clayton Wilson, our equipment manager, had to write something on his tape ankles before every game at a certain time. Like, it was routine.

quotes.speaker: Sam Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Mitchell on why he benched Karl-Anthony Towns as a rookie
quotes.excerpt: I need to teach this young man how to play the right way, play defense.
quotes.quote: I need to teach this young man how to play the right way, play defense. What were those early days with Karl-Anthony Towns like just trying to get him settled in as a rookie, figuring out the right way to play and get established here?

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: I remember there was one game where you sat him down in the fourth quarter. And afterward, it was, 'Sam, he's the number one overall pick, why is he not in in the fourth quarter?' And you said, 'I need to teach this young man how to play the right way, play defense.' What were those early days with Karl-Anthony Towns like just trying to get him settled in as a rookie, figuring out the right way to play and get established here?

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Mitchell
text_blocks.text: He was awesome. First of all, he's an unbelievable, nice young man. Just exceptional. He loves basketball. He cares about his teammates. It was easy to coach Karl. Now, the thing you have to do with a guy that talented, every now and then you got to rein them in a little bit. You just have to rein them in a little bit.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the Timberwolves' ownership transition
quotes.excerpt: Alex Rodriguez and Mark Lore closed on majority ownership and they reached out. It was very humbling.
quotes.quote: About a year ago today, we were celebrating the second Stanley Cup win that we had in Florida in the NHL. And Alex Rodriguez and Mark Lore closed on majority ownership and they reached out. It was very humbling. Literally, we were celebrating on the beach with the Stanley Cup and like that that Monday, they gave me a call saying they would love to chat with me.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the Timberwolves' arena project
quotes.excerpt: They want to build a new arena, they're hungry, they have a great sports market.
quotes.quote: The owner that I worked for in Florida was very close to. I worked with him before sports. He's been like a second father to me and he's like, 'Listen, this is a great opportunity. It's new ownership, they want to build a new arena, they're hungry, they have a great sports market.'

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the timeline for a new arena
quotes.excerpt: This is something we want to get done in the next five or six years.
quotes.quote: This is something we want to get done in the next five or six years. And if we can do it sooner, we would. But I mentioned this publicly, once you go shovel to ground, it's a three-year process easily. So there's always going to be hurdles, especially when you have the public-private partnership.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the arena's multi-use potential
quotes.excerpt: We do want to have as much real estate around the arena to have a multi-use.
quotes.quote: We do want to have as much real estate around the arena to have a multi-use. But at this at this juncture, I wouldn't sacrifice a downtown arena for like more acreage in a suburb at this point. We still that can change over the next year or two, but our priority is to try to find something in downtown Minneapolis.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the Timberwolves' arena and ticket pricing
quotes.excerpt: Pricing was at the bottom of the league and we've now had six straight seasons of playoffs.
quotes.quote: The team was bad for about 20 years, more or less, and pricing was at the bottom of the league and we've now had six straight seasons of playoffs. And a lot of times management teams and ownership groups, you know, fill the building up because the team's playing better, but they're not adjusting the pricing. So the increases that we've done is just about level setting and getting closer to, you know, we're at the 30 teams, we were 27th in the league in pricing.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the differences between NBA and NHL business
quotes.excerpt: The business sides are are pretty similar. Season tickets, media rights, sponsorships, the major revenue line items.
quotes.quote: The business sides are are pretty similar. Season tickets, media rights, sponsorships, the major revenue line items, very similar. Just the scale of the NBA. It blows my mind. They're looking at doing an NBA league in Europe. That billion dollar plus valuations. NHL was great, but the the US and Canadian teams are just starting to get over a billion now.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the importance of season ticket holders
quotes.excerpt: The season ticket holders make up 70% of the arenas in the NHL.
quotes.quote: The season ticket holders make up 70% of the arenas in the NHL. And then there's maybe half season ticket holders, quarter plans, but it's hard to get single game buyers that aren't like die-hard fans that didn't play the game or the kids play the game. It's hard to just appeal to someone that's just a sports fan.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the NBA's global scale
quotes.excerpt: We have bench players that have more social media followers than like the stars that we had.
quotes.quote: The global scale, the the number of fans. I mean, we have bench players that have more social media followers than like the stars that we had in the NHL. Like, I know Rob Dillingham's no longer with us, but his his social media, you know, engagement was more than Connor McDavid or Sasha Barkov in the NHL. And it goes to show you that even though he wasn't playing much, he only had one year in college, just the way he appealed to fans is his lifestyle brand that he had.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the Timberwolves' ownership and management
quotes.excerpt: They see Tim and I as like their ownership reps on the ground.
quotes.quote: They're really empowering to me and Tim Connelly. You know, they see Tim and I as like their ownership reps on the ground. Tim obviously on the basketball side, me and the business side. I would say Tim and I talk every single day. We talk to each other a lot more and then we bring decisions to Mark and Alex when we feel that they they need to opine on.

quotes.speaker: Matthew Caldwell
quotes.summary_phrase: Matthew Caldwell on the Timberwolves' arena process
quotes.excerpt: There's a lot that happens with securing the right site, working on the lease that we have.
quotes.quote: There's a lot that happens with securing the right site, working on the lease that we have here, working with the mayor's office on, you know, how we would have a new arrangement and new arena. There's nothing that I can like, you know, opine on, but do know that I'm not like kicking the can down the road and saying this is a pipe dream.
